proofs.proof_tex:
For a fixed eligible pair \((g,k)\), the definition of \(r_{gk}\) is an
exact equality.  The eligible estimator and target satisfy, respectively,
\[
 \widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\widehat\tau_{gk},
 \qquad
 \tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\tau_{gk}.
\]
The second equality follows from \(N_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}n_g\) and the
definition of \(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\).  Subtracting these equalities and
substituting the exact block decompositions gives
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}
   \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
All sums are finite.  Hence their order may be interchanged.  The definition
of the exact aggregated coefficient gives
\[
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}b_{gk,q}=c_{kq},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives \(s_k>0\).
Since \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), division by \(s_k\) yields
\[
 s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\sum_q a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q}
  +s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Comparison with the definition of \(\rho_{n,k}\) proves both the coordinate
identity and the displayed formula for \(\rho_{n,k}\); stacking the finite
collection of coordinates proves the vector identity.

On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), positivity of \(n_g/N_k\), the triangle inequality,
and the definition of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty
 &\le \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}|r_{gk}|\\
 &\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\\
 &=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to justify the finite probability statement in the stated source
submodel.  Apply \(\texttt{lem:choi-yuan-one-block-remainder}\) separately to
each eligible block.  In the notation of that cited proposition, the missing
group size is \(\vartheta_o=n_g\), the block dimensions are \(N_o=N_{gk}\)
and \(T_o=T_g\), and the proposition's three displayed remainder terms are
exactly those collected in \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  For a treated row
\(i\in I_g\), Proposition A.4 writes the imputation error as its donor-column
linear term, its treated-row pre-period linear term, and an entry remainder
\(\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}\).  Since
\[
 Y_{i,g+k}-m^0_{i,g+k}-\tau_{i,g+k}=e_{i,g+k},
\]
subtracting the imputation expansion and averaging over \(i\in I_g\) gives
the displayed block expansion with
\[
 r_{gk}=-\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}.
\]
Thus \(\max_{i\in I_g}|\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\)
implies \(|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  The uniform block ratios in
the source submodel and the common constants in the frozen class make the
constant in the cited one-block bound common to eligible blocks once \(n\) is
sufficiently large.  Consequently,
\[
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}
 \le C_0\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
Boole's inequality over the finite set of eligible pairs now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 &\le\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}\\
 &\le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is only a finite union bound.  None of the frozen assumptions forces its
right-hand side to tend to zero, which is why the theorem makes no stronger
stochastic-order claim.

Write \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\).  The denominator in
\(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) is finite only when \(h_{\min}>0\), so
every oracle average in the statement is well defined.  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\),
\(E_{P_n}[e_{it}^2]=\sigma_i^2\) for \(t\in H_i\).  We first prove the
uniform concentration claim directly from the sub-Gaussian assumption.

The definition of the \(\psi_2\)-norm and
\(\|e_{it}\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\sigma_i\) imply, after increasing a constant
depending only on \(C_e\), that
\[
 E_{P_n}\exp\{e_{it}^2/(C_2\sigma_i^2)\}\le2.
\]
For every integer \(m\ge1\), the elementary inequality
\(y^m\le m!e^y\) for \(y\ge0\) therefore gives
\[
 E_{P_n}|e_{it}|^{2m}\le2m!(C_2\sigma_i^2)^m.
\]
Let \(U_{it}=e_{it}^2-\sigma_i^2\).  Centeredness of \(U_{it}\), the last
display, \((x+y)^m\le2^{m-1}(x^m+y^m)\), and
\(\sigma_i\le\bar\sigma\) imply that, for every \(m\ge2\),
\[
 E_{P_n}|U_{it}|^m\le m!(C_3\bar\sigma^2)^m.
\]
Expanding the moment-generating function and using
\(E_{P_n}U_{it}=0\), for \(|\lambda|\le(2C_3\bar\sigma^2)^{-1}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_n}e^{\lambda U_{it}}
 &=1+\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda^mE_{P_n}U_{it}^m}{m!}\\
 &\le1+\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}(|\lambda|C_3\bar\sigma^2)^m
 \le\exp(C_4\lambda^2\bar\sigma^4).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For fixed \(i\), the variables \(\{U_{it}:t\in H_i\}\) are independent by
\(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\).  Multiplying their moment-generating
functions and optimizing the exponential Markov bound over the admissible
\(\lambda\) yields, for every \(y\ge0\),
\[
 P_n\!\left\{
 |\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|>
 C_5\bar\sigma^2\left(\sqrt{y/h_i}+y/h_i\right)
 \right\}\le2e^{-y}.
\]
Indeed, use \(\lambda\) proportional to
\(\min\{\sqrt{y/(h_i\bar\sigma^4)},1/\bar\sigma^2\}\) in the upper tail
and \(-\lambda\) in the lower tail.  Taking
\(y=\log(2N)+x\), using \(h_i\ge h_{\min}\), and applying Boole's inequality
over \(i\le N\) proves the first display in the statement after absorbing
\(\bar\sigma^2\) into \(C_1\).  Taking fixed large \(x\) proves the displayed
uniform \(O_{P_n}\) rate.

Put \(v_n=\sqrt{\log(2N)/h_{\min}}\).  Assumption
\(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) states
\[
 v_n\log^2(2K)\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
It also implies \(v_n\to0\).  Hence
\[
 (v_n+v_n^2)\log^2(2K)
 \le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}(1+v_n)\longrightarrow0,
\]
which proves the asserted \(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) oracle-variance rate.

For \(t\in H_i\), the observed cell is untreated, so the observation equation
gives \(Y_{it}=m^0_{it}+e_{it}\).  Therefore
\(\widehat e_{it}=e_{it}-d_{it}\), and exact expansion gives
\[
 \widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2
 =-\frac2{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}
   +\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and the definition of \(d_i\) yield
\[
 \left|h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}\right|
 \le\left(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i.
\]
The contamination inequality follows by the triangle inequality.  Notice that
no frozen assumption bounds \(d_i\), so this exact inequality cannot be
promoted to a feasible variance rate.

We finally prove score stability.  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\), \(\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\).  The
definitions of \(a_{kq}\), \(s_k\), and \(\Omega_{kk}\), together with
\(s_k>0\) from \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\), give
\[
 \|a_k\|_2^2=\sum_q a_{kq}^2
 =s_k^{-2}\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_u^2
 =s_k^{-2}\Omega_{kk}=1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q},
 \qquad
 \frac{\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_qa_{kq}a_{k'q}.
\]
Writing \(u_k=\widehat b_k-a_k\), the difference of the two inner products is
\[
 \langle u_k,a_{k'}\rangle+\langle a_k,u_{k'}\rangle
 +\langle u_k,u_{k'}\rangle.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\|a_k\|_2=1\) show that its
absolute value is at most \(h+h+h^2=\delta_h\), proving the covariance
inequality.

Set \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  The diagonal case gives
\(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  If \(\delta_h<1\), then
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}>0\), and
\[
 |t_k-1|=\frac{|t_k^2-1|}{t_k+1}
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}}.
\]
In particular, \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) is well defined.  Since
\(t_kt_{k'}\in[1-\delta_h,1+\delta_h]\), since
\(|\Sigma_{kk'}|\le1\) by Cauchy--Schwarz, and since the already proved
covariance discrepancy is at most \(\delta_h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}-\Sigma_{kk'}|
 &\le\frac{\delta_h}{t_kt_{k'}}
 +|\Sigma_{kk'}|\left|\frac1{t_kt_{k'}}-1\right|\\
 &\le\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 +\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 =\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves every claimed consequence while leaving the unprovided stochastic
score rate explicit.

Because \(s_k^2=\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_q^2\) and
\(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), assumption
\(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives
\[
 \sum_qa_{kq}^2=1.
\]
Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\) imply that the sign-expanded vectors
\(X_q\) are independent and centered.  Since
\(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^2=1\), for each of their \(p=2K\) coordinates,
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2=\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1.
\]
Their normalized sum has coordinate list
\((S_{n,0},\ldots,S_{n,K-1},-S_{n,0},\ldots,-S_{n,K-1})\), so its maximum
is \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\).  Finally,
\(\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\) and \(|a_{kq}|\le L_n(K)\) prove
the stated envelope.

We now verify the quantitative input to
\(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-approximation-maxima}\).  In the notation of that
cited theorem, let
\[
 M_\ell=\max_{j\le p}
 \left(m^{-1}\sum_qE_{P_n}|X_{qj}|^\ell\right)^{1/\ell}.
\]
Uniform sub-Gaussian moments and \(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_3^3
 &\le C m^{1/2}\max_k\sum_q|a_{kq}|^3
 \le C m^{1/2}L_n(K),\\
 M_4^4
 &\le C m\max_k\sum_qa_{kq}^4
 \le C mL_n(K)^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, a union bound applied to the sub-Gaussian tails of
\(\epsilon_q\), and to the Gaussian comparison summands used in the cited
theorem, gives its upper function the bound
\[
 u(\gamma)\le C\sqrt mL_n(K)
 \sqrt{\log(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)}.
\]
If \(p=2\), duplicate either sign-expanded coordinate; this leaves the maximum
unchanged and permits the cited theorem's convention \(p\ge3\).  Substitution
in Theorem 2.2 of that source yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_z|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}|\\
 &\quad\le C\left[
 m^{-1/8}(M_3^{3/4}\vee M_4^{1/2})
 \log^{7/8}(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)
 +m^{-1/2}\log^{3/2}(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)u(\gamma)+\gamma\right]\\
 &\quad\le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma),
 \end{aligned}
\]
because the first term is bounded by
\(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\}^{1/8}\) and the second by
\(CL_n(K)\log^2(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\).  No lower eigenvalue of
\(\Sigma_n\) is used: only the unit coordinate variances enter the cited
theorem.

We next transfer from the linear statistic to feasible studentization.  Put
\(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  By
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), on \(\mathcal A_n(C)\),
\[
 \max_k|\rho_{n,k}|\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\), on
\(\mathcal B_n(h)\), \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  When
\(\delta_h\le1/2\), the proof of that theorem also gives
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}\) and
\(|t_k^{-1}-1|\le\delta_h\).  Hence, on the intersection of the two events,
the reverse triangle inequality yields
\[
 \left|
 \max_k|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|-\max_k|S_{n,k}|
 \right|
 \le\delta_h\max_k|S_{n,k}|
 +\sqrt2C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]

The same sub-Gaussian moment-generating-function calculation used above,
now with \(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\), gives, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|>C_4\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}\}\le\delta_h
\]
after choosing \(C_4\) depending only on \(C_e\).  On the complementary
event the preceding perturbation is at most
\[
 v_n=C_5\{\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}
 +C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\}.
\]
Corollary 2.1 of
\(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-anti-concentration}\), applied to the finite
sign-expanded Gaussian vector with unit marginal variances, gives
\[
 \sup_zP\{|M_n^Z-z|\le v_n\}
 \le C_6v_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}.
\]
Sandwiching the feasible event between the linear events with thresholds
\(z-v_n\) and \(z+v_n\), and then using the already proved Gaussian
approximation, incurs the tail probability \(\delta_h\) and the
anti-concentration term
\[
 C_7\left\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}\right\}.
\]
For \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\), elementary logarithm bounds give
\[
 \delta_h+\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}
 \le C_8\left[\delta_h\log(2p)
 +\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}\right].
\]
Indeed, use \(\sqrt{ab}\le a\) for \(a\ge b>0\), split
\(\log(2p/\delta_h)\), and use
\(x\log(1/x)\le Cx^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/x)\}^{2/3}\) on
\(0<x\le1/2\).  Enlarging \(C_3\) in the definition of
\(\mathfrak c_n(h)\) therefore proves
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_z\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_k\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma)+P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\qquad+C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]

For the multiplier part, conditional on \(Y\), Gaussianity and independence
of \(\xi_q\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q,
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_{k'}}\xi_q
 \mathrel{\Big|}Y\right)
 =\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}.
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi\), conditionally on the data, is exactly the maximum absolute
coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), the
covariance theorem gives
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}\le4\delta_h.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-comparison-maxima}\) to the two
sign-expanded Gaussian vectors gives
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le C_3\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}.
\]
The cited comparison permits singular covariance matrices and therefore
retains the full staircase dependence.

Let \(F_Z\) be the distribution function of \(M_n^Z\).  The cited
anti-concentration inequality implies that \(F_Z\) is continuous.  On
\(\mathcal B_n(h)\), if \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), the
conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(W_n^\xi\) lies between the
\((1-\alpha-\mathfrak c_n(h))\)- and
\((1-\alpha+\mathfrak c_n(h))\)-quantiles of \(F_Z\).  Apply the feasible
distribution bound at these two deterministic quantiles and lose at most
\(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\) once more.  The observed-statistic bound already
contains one copy of \(\mathfrak c_n(h)\), and the quantile comparison adds a
second.  This proves the displayed finite coverage inequality.  When \(h=0\),
the scale perturbation and covariance discrepancy are exactly zero, so the
same conclusions hold with \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\) by direct substitution.

Finally, \(\texttt{ass:cell-leverage}\) implies
\(L_n(K)^2\log^7(pm)\to0\).  One may choose \(\gamma_n\downarrow0\) slowly
enough that
\(L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma_n)\to0\); the preceding formula then
shows \(\mathfrak g_n(\gamma_n)\to0\).  Assumption
\(\texttt{ass:uniform-remainder-envelope}\) gives
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\).  If
\(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\), then \(\delta_{h_n}\log(2p)\to0\) and
\[
 \delta_{h_n}\log^2(p/\delta_{h_n})\to0,
\]
because both \(x\log^2(1/x)\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\) and the assumed
\(\delta_{h_n}\log^2(2p)\to0\) hold.  Hence
\(\mathfrak c_n(h_n)\to0\).  Together with the two explicitly assumed
failure-probability limits, every term in the finite bound vanishes, proving
the conditional corollary and no stronger one.

added_lemmas.statement: For one Choi--Yuan missing block with dimensions \(N_o\) and \(T_o\), missing-group size \(\vartheta_o\), i.i.d. centered homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, incoherence, signal, spectral-size, and missing-block conditions as stated in their Appendix A, Proposition A.4 gives, with probability at least \(1-O(\min\{N_o^{-9},T_o^{-9}\})\), a simultaneous entrywise linear expansion of every target imputation error into its donor-column and observed-row terms, with the maximum entry remainder bounded by a common constant times the three-term expression used here as \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) after setting \((N_o,T_o,\vartheta_o)=(N_{gk},T_g,n_g)\).

attestation.note: Verified directly against the Proposition A.4 environment and Appendix A assumptions in the arXiv v1 TeX source; the carrier states only the one-block conclusion used here.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the published one-block remainder premise used only for the source-submodel finite union bound.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited proposition is not a growing-block or heterogeneous-noise result.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the blockwise failure probability in thm:uniform-influence.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) be independent centered random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), let \(X=m^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^m x_j\), and let \(Y\) be the centered Gaussian vector with the same covariance.  If every coordinate of \(X\) has variance between fixed positive constants, then Theorem 2.2 bounds the Kolmogorov distance between \(\max_{\ell\le p}X_\ell\) and \(\max_{\ell\le p}Y_\ell\) by
\[
 C\left[m^{-1/8}(M_3^{3/4}\vee M_4^{1/2})\log^{7/8}(pm/\gamma)
 +m^{-1/2}\log^{3/2}(pm/\gamma)u(\gamma)+\gamma\right]
\]
for every \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), with \(M_3,M_4\) and \(u(\gamma)\) defined in that theorem; Corollary 2.1 records the corresponding vanishing approximation under its leading moment regimes.  No restriction is imposed on correlations among coordinates.

attestation.note: Verified directly against the Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.1 environments in the arXiv TeX source.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the degenerate-covariance-safe Gaussian approximation used for the sign-expanded event score.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited theorem is generic probability substrate; the adaptation to the event-by-cell coefficients is proved in this note.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the oracle Gaussian approximation term in thm:uniform-multiplier-band.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(V\) and \(Y\) be centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), assume the coordinate variances of \(Y\) are bounded above and away from zero, and put \(\Delta_0=\max_{j,\ell}|\operatorname{Cov}(V_j,V_\ell)-\operatorname{Cov}(Y_j,Y_\ell)|\).  Lemma 3.1 gives
\[
 \sup_z\left|P\{\max_jV_j\le z\}-P\{\max_jY_j\le z\}\right|
 \le C\Delta_0^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\Delta_0)\}^{2/3},
\]
without a positive-minimum-eigenvalue requirement.

attestation.note: Verified directly against the Lemma 3.1 environment in the arXiv TeX source.

added_lemmas.justification: This converts the deterministic maximum covariance error into a conditional Gaussian distribution error.
added_lemmas.gap: The application must still prove the covariance discrepancy for the frozen score construction.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the covariance-comparison term in thm:uniform-multiplier-band.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a separable centered Gaussian process with unit pointwise variances and almost surely finite supremum, Theorem 2.1 bounds the Levy concentration function of the supremum at radius \(\varepsilon\) by \(4\varepsilon\) times one plus its expected supremum.  Corollary 2.1 gives the same bound for the supremum of the absolute value.  For a finite \(p\)-coordinate Gaussian vector this implies
\[
 \sup_zP\left\{\left|\max_{j\le p}|Z_j|-z\right|\le\varepsilon\right\}
 \le C\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(2p)}.
\]

attestation.note: Verified directly against the Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1 environments in the arXiv TeX source.

added_lemmas.justification: This turns the event-score and studentization perturbations into Kolmogorov and coverage errors.
added_lemmas.gap: The event-specific perturbation radius is derived in this note.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the anti-concentration terms in thm:uniform-multiplier-band.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(n\).  For \(g\in E_k\), let \(b_{gk,q}\) denote the expression inside square brackets in the definition of \(c_{kq}\), let
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),
 \qquad
 \tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and define the exact block remainder \(r_{gk}\) by
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk}.
\]
Then the eligible-unit aggregation obeys the exact eventwise identity
\[
 D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
For \(C>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)=\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\), which is positive under \(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\), and define the oracle residual variance
\[
 \widetilde\sigma_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2.
\]
There is a constant \(C_1<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\) and \(\bar\sigma\), such that, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}}P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|>
 C_1\left[\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}\right]\right\}\le2e^{-x}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 =O_{P_n}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}\right)
 =o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.  For
\[
 d_{it}=\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it},
 \qquad
 d_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2,
\]
the feasible residual variance has the exact contamination bound
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2|
 \le2\left(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i+d_i^2.
\]

\[

 \qquad

 \left\{\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}

\]
and \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), with \(\delta_h=2h+h^2<1\),
\[
 \max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}\le\delta_h,
 \qquad
 \max_k\left|\frac{\widehat s_k}{s_k}-1\right|
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}},
\]
and

 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
\]

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\), \(p=2K\), \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\), and
\[
 S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\epsilon_q.
\]
Indexing \(q\) arbitrarily, sign-expand
\[
 X_q=\sqrt m\,(a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q,
 -a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,-a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q)\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Then \(m^{-1/2}\sum_qX_q\) has maximum \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\), every coordinate has variance one, and \(\max_{q,j}\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\sqrt m L_n(K)\).  For \(0<\gamma<1/2\), put
\[
 \mathfrak g_n(\gamma)=C_1\left[
 \{L_n(K)^2\log^7(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)\}^{1/8}
 +L_n(K)\log^2(((p\vee3)m)/\gamma)+\gamma\right],
\]
where \(C_1\) depends only on \(C_e\).  If \(M_n^Z=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|\), then
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}|
 \le\mathfrak g_n(\gamma).
\]
Fix \(C>0\) and \(h\ge0\).  Let \(\mathcal A_n(C)\) be as in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), let \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\), and put \(\delta_h=2h+h^2\).  There are constants \(C_2,C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such that whenever \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \mathfrak c_n(h):=C_3\delta_h^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3},
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_k\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le \mathfrak g_n(\gamma)+P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}
 +C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), conditionally on \(Y\), \(W_n^\xi\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\), and
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le \mathfrak c_n(h).
\]
If \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), then the band satisfies the finite coverage bound
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}
 \text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\\
 &\quad\le 1\wedge\Big[\mathfrak g_n(\gamma)
 +P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}+2P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}+C_2\{C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2p)}
 +\delta_h\log(2p)\}+2\mathfrak c_n(h)\Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Define \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\).  Consequently, along any complete array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), if for some fixed \(C\) and some deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\),
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(2p)\to0,
\]
then the conditional multiplier distribution consistently estimates the Gaussian comparison law and the displayed band has coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\).  This corollary is conditional on the two displayed failure probabilities; the frozen class alone does not make them vanish.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Unconditional class-uniform coverage does not follow while the simultaneous remainder and feasible score failure probabilities are uncontrolled.  =\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,
 \qquad

\]
For \(C>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)=\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
 \{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}.

\[

 \le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.

proposed.justification: This theorem supplies the exact bridge from blockwise debiasing to the adoption-aligned event score and records precisely what a simultaneous source-level remainder event would deliver.
proposed.gap: Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 is one-block and i.i.d. homoskedastic; direct aggregation over growing eligible blocks yields a finite union bound, not a class-uniform stochastic remainder rate.

prose_updates.tldr: The eligible-cohort Choi--Yuan blocks aggregate exactly into one event-by-cell score, whose covariance contains every shared staircase cell.  What is currently proved is an exact influence identity, a deterministic Choi--Yuan remainder implication with an honest finite union bound in the source i.i.d. homoskedastic submodel, oracle unit-variance concentration, exact feasible-score stability, and a finite-error Gaussian-multiplier theorem.  Growing-curve coverage follows only along arrays for which both the simultaneous block-remainder failure probability and the feasible score-loading failure probability vanish at the displayed rates.  The frozen assumptions alone do not establish either probability limit.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR results provide one-block, entrywise, scalar, or fixed-functional inference, while staggered DiD results provide simultaneous paths under parallel trends.  No located result supplies a growing adoption-aligned Choi--Yuan block remainder theorem under unit heteroskedasticity together with the rowwise score-loading rate needed by the frozen plug-in covariance.
project_justification.niche: The useful intermediate object is a primitive-cell event score with an exact shared-cell covariance and a finite-error inference theorem that exposes, rather than assumes, the two missing simultaneous controls.
project_justification.fill: The note fixes eligible-unit weights, aggregates the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients algebraically, proves the full staircase covariance, concentrates the oracle unit variances, and bounds covariance, scale, and correlation errors deterministically by \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).  A sign-expanded Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato approximation, singular-covariance-safe Gaussian comparison, and Gaussian anti-concentration yield an explicit coverage bound containing \(P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}\), \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\), the Choi--Yuan remainder perturbation, and the score-stability terms.  This is an actionable conditional protocol, not an unconditional theorem over the entire frozen class.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed feasible implementation uses exact blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals on \(\mathcal V_n\), unit-level residual variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\).  The oracle variance component is uniformly concentrated, while the imputation contamination and the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) loading discrepancy remain explicit diagnostics through \(d_i\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, Proposition A.4 on pages 35--36 of arXiv:2308.02364v1, provide a one-block entrywise expansion under i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise with failure probability of order \(\min\{N_o^{-9},T_o^{-9}\}\).  Aggregating that result over a growing collection of eligible blocks yields only the finite union bound displayed here; their Supplement G.2 does not supply a growing-block theorem.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, Theorem 3.1 and Theorem C.2, analyze a fixed group functional under additional conditions and do not control the frozen leave-one-cell-out contamination or a growing rowwise score-loading error.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.1, and Lemma 3.1, supply the high-dimensional Gaussian approximation and covariance comparison used in the finite-error theorem without requiring nonsingular correlation.  Their confidence-band paper, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands}, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, supplies the anti-concentration step.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate event-time aggregation and the right-to-carry application, but do not establish the missing feasible growing-path rates.  Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, give simultaneous staggered paths under conditional parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion.  Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, and Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, provide entrywise or scalar low-rank inference, not this growing event-curve transfer.
prose_updates.interpretation: For an empirical right-to-carry event curve, the common critical value is conditionally calibrated once the realized score discrepancy is small and a simultaneous block-remainder guarantee is justified.  The exact covariance formula prevents treating reused donor or pre-treatment cells as independent, but it does not by itself certify the plug-in covariance.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen Choi--Yuan ratios control a published one-block perturbation expression, not a simultaneous heterogeneous block event.  The direct source union bound need not vanish as the number of cohort-horizon blocks grows.  Separately, variance replication concentrates \(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\), but no frozen premise controls \(\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it}\) or the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) error of \(\widehat c\).  Therefore neither \(\|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) nor \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}(\log^{-2}(2K))\) is claimed over the full class.  The attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remains open, and the balanced rank-one diagnostic gives no converse for the coarse published envelope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target remains the eligible-cohort unit-share event curve under exact low rank, deterministic staggered adoption, overlap through the donor and pre-period Gram conditions, and independent centered row-heteroskedastic sub-Gaussian cell noise.  The exact eventwise score and staircase covariance are unconditional algebraic results under their stated definitions.  Feasible inference is a finite-error result whose bound displays the simultaneous remainder and score-loading failure probabilities; asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) coverage is asserted only on subclasses or individual arrays where those probabilities vanish and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\).  Serial dependence, approximate rank, tuning selection, and a proof of those two growing-block rates remain outside the settled scope.
